newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk plant gets new director.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk plant gets new director.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group has changed the leadership at its flagship combine as part of a restructuring plan to solve the plant's financial crisis, a Norilsk spokesman said on Friday.
Anatoly Komrakov said Leonid Galperin, formerly vice-president of Moscow's Zil auto works, had replaced Nikolai Abramov as general director of the Norilsky Nikel mining and enriching complex.
Abramov has become deputy director of the RAO Norilsky Nikel group, which is headed by Alexander Khloponin.
Khloponin is also a board member of Uneximbank, the Russian commercial bank that controls a 38 percent stake in Norilsk and is trying to bring the combine out of financial crisis.
"The change in leadership is related to the situation that we inherited," Komrakov said, referring to the combine's debts of around 500 million roubles.
He also said the plant would see more management changes, particularly in its financial department.
Norilsk is Russia's largest producer of nickel, copper, platinum, palladium and platinum group metals.
